angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 463,382 km at 157.68 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.3421 +/- 0.0121 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 157.68 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.666066 solar radii from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-7333 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract): 463,382 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.748 (0.708 to 0.788) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4586.87 K from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7333 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7333 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-7333.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.665, rounded to two decimals
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-7333 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.75937, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 1704081330420181632, flags_flame 00: age_flame 0.8905312 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 0.2 to 3.302063)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
